original.title: A sublinear record-drop envelope controls ordering error
assumptions: μ_n=d(n)−max_{r<n}d(r)≥−b(n), with b nonnegative and nondecreasing.
Canonical all-candidate envelope supplier remains open.

exactAuditedStatement: For injective positive integer d with n<d(n)<=2n+1, M_n=max_{r<n}d(r), and nonnegative nondecreasing integer b satisfying d(n)>=M_n-b(n), F_n=#{r>n:d(r)<d(n)}<=b(2n+1), B_n=#{r<n:d(r)>d(n)}<=b(n), and|F_n-B_n|<=b(2n+1).
hypotheses: Use M_0=0; envelope holds for all relevant indices.
No canonical constant/logarithmic envelope is proved.
independentDerivationAndChecks: Backward inversion values are distinct integers in(d(n), M_n], at most M_n-d(n)<=b(n); if d(n)>=M_n the set is empty.
Forward contributor r obeys r<d(r)<d(n)<=2n+1. Its earlier record M_r>=d(n), so d(r)>=d(n)-b(r)>=d(n)-b(2n+1). Distinct integers in[d(n)-b(2n+1), d(n))number at most b(2n+1).
The absolute difference of two nonnegative counts is bounded by their maximum; monotonicity of b compares the backward bound. At n=0 the F/B sets are empty and formulas remain valid.
Any J-based central-discrepancy consumer additionally requires the exact algebraic I3 identity and a supplied J bound; the envelope theorem supplies neither a canonical b nor J bound.
